newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close mixed, eye on Friday's GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close mixed, eye on Friday's GDP data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed on Thursday, with firmer U.S. Treasuries providing some strength as investors turned their attention to Friday's Canadian and U.S. GDP data, analysts said.

"There's just nothing going on. We know that there's all of these numbers coming and we're just sort of sitting back and trying to roll with the punches," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.15 to C$108.10 to yield 7.302 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond rose 13/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 42 basis points from 41 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
Canadian and U.S. bond investors had focused their attention on today's testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan before the U.S. Senate Finance Committee.
However, Greenspan's comments had little impact on the markets and investors are now looking to economic data for clues to the direction of interest rates.
Statistics Canada on Friday reports Canada's real gross domestic product at factor cost for November.
In the United States, real gross domestic product data for the fourth quarter is due on Friday.
"The next key focal points will be the GDP report tomorrow for the U.S. and the U.S. employment data coming out next Friday," said Rob Palombi, senior fixed income analyst with MMS International.

In other news, the Bank of Canada and several bond brokers are now recognizing new two- and three-year Government of Canada benchmark bonds. The new two-year benchmark is Canada's 5.75 percent bond due March, 1999, replacing the 6.25 percent bond due September, 1998.
The new three-year benchmark is the 5.5 percent bond due February, 2000, replacing the 6.5 percent bond due August, 1999.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.15 to C$102.60 to yield 6.634 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 6/32 to yield 6.60 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds was three basis points, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.87 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.18 percent.
